summary: Saudi Arabia is reportedly preparing a large-scale military offensive against Yemen with detailed operational plans, while Ansar Allah has consolidated control over strategic mountains near Bab al-Mandab despite heavy airstrikes. Houthis have declared Saudi airspace unsafe for commercial aviation, signaling major escalation. Simultaneously, IDF conducted multiple operations in southern Syria's buffer zone and thwarted attacks in the West Bank including a ramming attempt and knife assault.

Houthis warned all airlines that Saudi airspace is unsafe, representing dangerous escalation possibly due to heavy frontal losses. (Source: @shin_persian/10785)
IDF eliminated Nukhba platoon commander Ibrahim Abu Uweimer in Nuseirat airstrike; he participated in Oct 7 massacre and planned new attacks. (Source: @almogboker78/18361)

sections.threat_assessment: The convergence of Saudi offensive preparations in Yemen, Houthi airspace threats, and intensified IDF operations across Syria and the West Bank indicates a region-wide escalation trajectory. Ansar Allah's consolidation near Bab al-Mandab despite heavy airstrikes suggests improved defensive coordination and willingness to threaten global shipping. The Houthi airline warning represents a deliberate escalation to pressure Saudi Arabia economically and diplomatically. Simultaneously, persistent infiltration attempts in southern Syria test IDF buffer zone enforcement, while West Bank attacks demonstrate sustained militant capability. Iran's economic distress may incentivize proxy activation, though its cyber readiness claim suggests asymmetric response preferences.
